## CANDIDA URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS
A positive urine culture for candida usually reflects colonization. Treat
cystitis only if the patient has symptoms of urinary tract infection (e.g.
dysuria, frequency, urgency, and/or suprapubic tenderness) or if the patient
will undergo invasive urological manipulation
Asymptomatic candiduria in a patient with a urinary catheter should not be
treated without an additional indication. Removal of catheter is strongly
recommended. Contact Infectious Diseases for more information.
Neutropenic patients with asymptomatic candiduria should be assessed for
candidemia because they are at risk of dissemination. Obtain blood cultures and
assess potential sources of candidemia such as central venous catheters. Refer
to fungemia page for treatment recommendations.
[Fungemia Associated with Candida spp.](orzid2-gmenu-bacteremia-candida-spp)
## Treatment
## Inpatient

Patient undergoing invasive urological manipulation:
Fluconazole 400 mg (6 mg/kg) PO q24h ($) [R,DI] for 3 days before and 3 days
after procedure
< OR >
Fluconazole 400 mg (6 mg/kg) IV q24h ($) [R,DI] for 3 days before and 3 days
after procedure
Symptomatic candida cystitis:
Fluconazole 200 mg (3 mg/kg) PO q24h ($) [R,DI] for 14 days
< OR >
Fluconazole 200 mg (3 mg/kg) IV q24h ($) [R,DI] for 14 days
Pyelonephritis:
Fluconazole 400 mg (6 mg/kg) PO q24h ($) [R,DI] for 14 days
< OR >
Fluconazole 400 mg (6 mg/kg) IV q24h ($) [R,DI] for 14 days
Resistant candida:
Consult Infectious Diseases for treatment options
